title: Roundabouts & Mini-Roundabouts
whatItIs: Approach with MSM at every stage, give priority to traffic from the right unless signs, markings or lights say otherwise, and pick lane and signals by your exit.
keyFacts: Decide your exit early, use MSM at all stages and time your signals so they don't confuse others.
Give priority to traffic approaching from your right, unless signs, road markings or lights direct otherwise.

keyFacts.text: At a mini-roundabout all vehicles MUST pass round the central markings, except large vehicles that can't.

keyFacts: Mini-roundabouts are normally on roads with a 30 mph limit or less. Avoid U-turns at them.
Give priority to cyclists on the roundabout and don't try to overtake them within their lane.
Double or multiple mini-roundabouts: treat each one separately and give way to traffic from the right.

visual.caption: Lanes and signals at a four-way roundabout (Highway Code rule 186)

routes.label: 1st exit · turning left
steps: Signal left and approach in the left lane
Keep left and keep signalling left to leave

routes.label: 2nd exit · going ahead
steps: Select the appropriate lane: normally no signal
Signal left after passing the 1st exit

routes.label: 3rd exit · turning right
steps: Signal right and approach in the right lane
Keep right until you need to change lanes
Signal left after passing the 2nd exit

notes: Unless signs or markings show otherwise

a.label: Positioning: normal driving
points: Going ahead at a roundabout without lane markings
Fault: cutting across the normal road position

b.label: Positioning: lane discipline
points: Going ahead at a roundabout with lane markings
Fault: not keeping to the marked lane, or straddling lanes

onTheTest.question: Your pupil is taking the 3rd exit (to the right) at a roundabout with no signs or markings saying otherwise. When should they signal left?
options: On the approach to the roundabout
After passing the exit before the one they want
Only when they reach their exit
onTheTest.why: Rule 186: signal right and approach in the right-hand lane, then signal left after you have passed the exit before the one you want. DT1 records late exit signals at roundabouts.

onTheTest.question: A cyclist in the left-hand lane of a roundabout is signalling right. What is this most likely to mean?
options: They are about to move into the right-hand lane
They are continuing across or around the roundabout
They are leaving at the next exit
They have forgotten to cancel their signal
onTheTest.why: Rule 186: cyclists, horse riders and horse-drawn vehicles may stay in the left lane when continuing around, signalling right. Don't cut across them as you enter.

traps: Late exit signals are a DT1 timing fault: signal left once you have passed the exit before yours.
Even where markings let you enter without giving way, still look right before you join.
Others on the roundabout may not signal correctly or at all: watch their speed and position.
Long vehicles may straddle lanes or take a different course: give them plenty of room.
